reviewer_levers.name: Structural inequality and exclusion
reviewer_levers.note: Same cut as our Tackling Structural Exclusion. The reviewer folds redistribution (tax, land reform) into P1; we hold tax under F-52 Revenue and spending systems, land redistribution under F-38 and transfers under F-06, with TSE as the lens for who is reached.

reviewer_levers.name: Education, skills, digital and health capabilities
reviewer_levers.note: Our Knowledge and Long and healthy life groups. Household digital access sits in F-12 Skills for work; government digital delivery is F-53 and is not a capability of people.

reviewer_levers.name: Human security, social protection and resilience
reviewer_levers.note: Our Decent standard of living group carries HDR 1994's economic, food and personal security. Shock-responsive protection is split in our tree between the protection itself (F-06), the pre-arranged finance (F-40) and the relief operation (F-51).

reviewer_levers.name: Future generations, children and youth investment
reviewer_levers.note: The reviewer's P4 mixes early childhood (our F-11, a Knowledge family) with intergenerational stewardship (our whole Future Generations subpillar, measured as inclusive wealth). We keep them apart: early childhood is a capability lever; the FUT subpillar is about not shifting costs to the future.

reviewer_levers.name: Export-led growth, trade and global value chains
reviewer_levers.note: Our Reaching foreign markets and Foreign capital and networks groups; export upgrading itself is F-22 under Upgrading and innovation.

reviewer_levers.name: Domestic integration, connectivity and spatial development
reviewer_levers.note: Same cut as our Domestic Integration subpillar (WDR 2009). We agree with the reviewer's boundary: interagency coordination is F-48 under governance, never domestic integration.

reviewer_levers.name: Inclusive growth, SMEs and community enterprise
reviewer_levers.note: Our Growth That Includes subpillar, cut by the constraint (firm capability, finance, farm productivity, market access, jobs, mobility) rather than by firm size, which answers the reviewer's own warning that size is not productivity.

reviewer_levers.name: Innovation, technology, R&D and digital transformation
reviewer_levers.note: Our Upgrading and innovation group (Growth Report: importing ideas). Rules for data, cyber and AI are F-46 under adaptive governance; government digital delivery is F-53.

reviewer_levers.name: Environmental sustainability, conservation and circular economy
reviewer_levers.note: The reviewer keeps environment under Smarter Growth 'for operational convenience'. We place it under People-first as Future Generations, measured as natural capital, because the reviewer's own argument (ecological outcomes are independent ends) points there.

reviewer_levers.name: Resource, energy, food and water security
reviewer_levers.note: Not one group in our tree. Water allocation is F-16 (natural capital), food security F-07 (a household capability), energy supply F-26 (an infrastructure service), resource rents F-18 (public wealth). The reviewer's G6 bundles four different protected units; the reviewer's own boundary rule (code by protected unit) argues for our split.

reviewer_levers.name: International and regional cooperation
reviewer_levers.note: No family in our tree. Cooperation appears as levers inside the family whose outcome it serves (LV-105 trade agreements, LV-103 transit agreements, LV-084 cross-border water, LV-132 regional energy links) and otherwise as an instrument tag. We keep it that way: a cooperation agreement has no outcome of its own, which is the reviewer's own rule that instruments are not families.

reviewer_levers.name: Public sector reform, governance and anti-corruption
reviewer_levers.note: Spread across our Authorised flexibility (capacity), Accountability (transparency, horizontal checks) and Market rules groups. The reviewer's M1 is a residual bin; our split follows the Future-Ready Governance dimensions and WDR 2017.

reviewer_levers.name: Participation, collaboration and civic engagement
reviewer_levers.note: Participatory decision-making (F-47), client power and community voice (F-59) and reform coalitions (F-58). Cross-government coordination (F-48) is the reviewer's cross-cutting coherence lens, not M2.

reviewer_levers.name: Democratic reform, rights, cohesion and conflict reduction
reviewer_levers.note: Electoral accountability, social cohesion and trust, horizontal accountability; rights of excluded groups sit in TSE (F-03, F-04).

reviewer_levers.name: Strategic anticipation, adaptability and risk management
reviewer_levers.note: Our Anticipation and Adaptation subpillars, cut into sensing, buffers, foresight, planning, feedback and experimentation. The reviewer's M4 asks for 'a capability to revise', which is our F-44 and F-45 exactly.

reviewer_levers.name: Monitoring, evaluation, targets and performance management
reviewer_levers.note: Monitoring and corrective feedback (F-44) and statistics and data sharing (F-43). We agree with the reviewer's rule: data collection is not policy adjustment, hence F-43 and F-44 are separate.

reviewer_levers.name: Fiscal, budgetary and financial-sector reform
reviewer_levers.note: Revenue and spending systems (F-52), the public balance sheet (F-18) and finance for small borrowers (F-31). The reviewer's M6 mixes the state's fiscal capacity with financial-sector development; we keep financial-sector development under growth.

reviewer_levers.name: Local empowerment and area-based development
reviewer_levers.note: Local tiers and capacity (F-50), lagging regions and place-based development (F-29), participatory budgeting (F-47). We agree with the reviewer: location is not decentralised power, so F-29 (where) and F-50 (who decides) stay apart.
